claims.text: The special access designation was the Secretary of the Army's, above INSCOM. The deactivation letter asks HQDA to take 'the necessary actions ... to officially discontinue CENTER LANE as a Secretary of the Army designated Special Access Program', and every page of the project's paperwork carries the warning notice 'CENTER LANE SPECIAL ACCESS PROGRAM RESTRICT DISSEMINATION TO THOSE WITH VERIFIED ACCESS TO CATEGORY THREE (3)'.

claims.source: Memorandum, INSCOM CENTER LANE Project (U), 17 July 1984, CIA-RDP96-00788R001500100011-4, https://archive.org/download/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp96-00788r001500100011-4/cia-rdp96-00788r001500100011-4_djvu.txt ; letter of 2 March 1985, CIA-RDP96-00789R002100120002-4, https://archive.org/download/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp96-00789r002100120002-4/cia-rdp96-00789r002100120002-4_djvu.txt
claims.text: The transfer to DIA was INSCOM's own recommendation, not a DIA rescue after a congressional petition. In July 1984 INSCOM's commanding general wrote that 'INSCOM ... should discontinue our involvement with psychoenergetic research and operations', intended 'to cease INSCOM CENTER LANE Project operations on 30 Sept 1984', and asked for authority to permit 'timely and undisrupted transfer of (1) ICLP operations to a national agency such as DIA or NSA'. The letter of 2 March 1985 then notified HQDA of 'the deactivation of the INSCOM CENTER LANE Project, the attachment OPCON of CENTER LANE assets and resources to the Defense Intelligence Agency, and the retirement of CENTER LANE as an active project nickname'. Nothing opened mentions Vorona or a petition to Congress.

desc: CENTER LANE was the Army Intelligence and Security Command's designation for the operational remote-viewing unit from 1983, succeeding GRILL FLAME after the codename was compromised. It was run as an INSCOM special access programme with its own security classification guide - a detail worth holding onto, because it demonstrates that the US Army was willing to place a psychic-functioning programme inside SAP-level access controls. The renaming sequence itself is instructive for this board: GRILL FLAME to CENTER LANE to SUN STREAK to STARGATE, four names for one continuous effort across three agencies in seventeen years. Codeword churn on compromise is the standard tradecraft response, and it is the reason why chasing a single programme name through the record is a losing method. The effort persists; the label does not.
